name: Karimeen Pollichathu (Pearl Spot Fish)
instructions: 1. Marinate cleaned fish with chili powder, turmeric, pepper, lemon juice, and salt; let it rest for 20 minutes.
2. Lightly fry the marinated fish on a pan until half-cooked and set aside.
3. In the same pan, sauté onions, green chilies, ginger-garlic paste, and curry leaves until golden.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft, then stir in the remaining spices and coconut milk to create a thick masala paste.
5. Wilt the banana leaf over an open flame to soften it.
6. Place a spoonful of masala on the leaf, lay the fish over it, and top with more masala.
7. Fold the leaf into a parcel and secure with thread.
8. Pan-fry the wrapped fish parcel for 5-7 minutes on each side on low heat to steam-roast the fish inside the leaf.
description: Karimeen Pollichathu is a signature dish from the backwaters of Kerala, particularly associated with the Syrian Christian and coastal culinary traditions. It is famous for its unique cooking method of 'pollichathu' (roasting in a leaf), which preserves the fish's moisture and imparts a distinct smoky flavor from the toasted banana leaf.
